transcript:
[00:00] Marina Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. I think we'll run about an hour, right? Set aside sixty minutes. Uh, quick intros?
[00:12] Diane Morales: Hi, Diane here, Head of Partnerships at CloudArc. Thanks, Marina. We've got Arjun and Lena with us.
[00:18] Arjun Singh: Hey all, Arjun, sales ops. Morning, afternoon depending on where you are.
[00:22] Lena Wu: Lena, CTO. I'll jump in on the technical bits.
[00:26] Ethan Park: Ethan from Redwood, solutions engineering. I'll handle the perf and architecture Qs.
[00:30] Marina Patel: Great. Goal for today is to walk through CloudArc's near-term pipeline for the EU and US, identify 2–3 high-prop accounts for an immediate co-sell push, and surface any technical or legal gating so we can scope next steps.
[00:45] Diane Morales: Perfect. We have six active opps — three in the EU, two in North America, one APAC pilot. The EU ones are the highest ARR potential but also the stickiest from a compliance perspective.
[01:00] Marina Patel: Got it. Can you share the criteria that makes those EU opps high priority?
[01:04] Diane Morales: Sure, they're platform SaaS vendors, high token volumes, and they require strict data residency. Also, procurement timelines are usually 60–90 days. We're expecting Q3 close ideally.
[01:16] Marina Patel: Thanks. Quick question on success criteria — what would you need from Redwood to feel comfortable co-selling? Is it pricing, SSO, audit evidence, or a pilot with low-risk SLAs?
[01:28] Lena Wu: For technical teams it's a combo: SOC 2 type II evidence, KMS support for customer-managed keys, and the ability to run in our VPC or a private deployment. Latency SLOs are secondary but still important.
[01:40] Arjun Singh: Commercially, we need predictable gross-split math — partners want clear margins. Also clarity on renewal handling with dedicated accounts.
[01:49] Marina Patel: Understood. Ethan, could you talk through platform options at a high level — hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[01:56] Ethan Park: Yeah, quick run. So Redwood Hosted is the fastest on-ramp, good for low-friction PLG style integrations. Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity — predictable latency and throughput, dedicate GPUs, better for steady high throughput. And Redwood Private is V P C or on-prem — full isolation, customer-controlled networking and KMS.
[02:20] Diane Morales: When you say Dedicated, is that a multi-tenant pool or fully single-tenant? For some of our targets single-tenant is preferred.
[02:28] Ethan Park: Dedicated is per-customer reserved pools; you get logical isolation but it's still in the Redwood control plane. Private is the fully dedicated hardware option when you need single-tenant and strict network isolation.
[02:38] Diane Morales: Okay. Any differences in pricing model that we should flag for partner conversations?
[02:44] Marina Patel: Yes — Hosted is usage-based (per token), Dedicated has a commit/compute reservation plus lower unit costs, and Private is licensed + infra. For co-sell, we usually propose a blended margin model depending on who owns the invoicing and support. We'll share a partner pricing matrix.
[02:58] Arjun Singh: One of the EU accounts specifically asked about data residency and whether logs are persisted in US.
[03:04] Ethan Park: We have regionally-hosted endpoints and can pin inference to EU regions. Audit logs can be configured to retain in-region, and for Private we can guarantee customer-managed KMS so keys never leave the tenant. Caveat: some telemetry like platform metrics used for observability might be aggregated; we can scope that per-customer.
[03:26] Lena Wu: Can you confirm SOC2? They asked for Type II report.
[03:30] Marina Patel: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II. I'll attach the cert and the security overview. We'll send the security pack after the call.
[03:37] Diane Morales: Great.
[03:39] Marina Patel: Let's get into the six accounts — high-level notes: Account A (EU) — vertical: fintech, 5–7M ARR forecast, procurement Q3. Account B (EU) — healthcare analytics startup, requires ISO and residency. Account C (EU) — logistics platform, heavy token volumes. Account D (NA) — marketplace, medium ARR. Account E (NA) — edtech pilot, low-touch. Account F (APAC) — pilot only.
[04:05] Diane Morales: Yes that's correct. Account A is the one we want to push first, but they asked for a short pilot that proves latency under heavy concurrent traffic.
[04:14] Ethan Park: For that, we'd recommend a Dedicated baseline — we can model the concurrency and do a 2-hour perf run with your payload. I can run it in EU-west region on a medium reserved pool and capture p50/p95. We'll also instrument KV cache behavior.
[04:29] Lena Wu: When you say KV cache, we need clarity on caching of customer prompts and whether there's any retention risk. We can't have sensitive PII cached.
[04:36] Ethan Park: Absolutely. The runtime supports prefix/KV caching but it's configurable. For EU regulated workloads we can disable persistent caching or tune TTLs; we can also ensure the cache keys are ephemeral and encrypted. Sorry if I said K V cash earlier — that's the transcript robot for you.
[04:51] Marina Patel: (laughter) Classic. Diane, do you have any concerns on sales messaging? Often pricing vs latency is the trade we need to navigate.
[04:59] Diane Morales: Yeah, from partners' POV we need simple language: "predictable latency" and "enterprise controls" — they don't want to dive into whole infra details early in the funnel. Also we need an easy bundle for outbound — one pager that says "what problem we solve" and "typical economics".
[05:16] Marina Patel: We'll provide a co-sell one-pager and a partner cheat sheet. Also, we'll include IRQs around renewal splits — who does the upsell conversations.
[05:25] Arjun Singh: On splits, CloudArc prefers a referral + carve model for mid-market and joint invoice for enterprise. We need templates.
[05:33] Marina Patel: Noted. We'll include three recommended commercial motions in the deck.
[05:38] Diane Morales: From a timing perspective, if we can get the perf baseline and the deck in the next week we can coordinate an initial outreach the following week.
[05:46] Marina Patel: Ethan, is the perf run something you can start next week?
[05:49] Ethan Park: Yes — I can start a basic run with the sample payloads Arjun will send. I'll need a test dataset and any traffic shapes. Two hours should be enough to capture p50/p95 and token cost estimate.
[06:02] Arjun Singh: I'll upload a sanitized sample and a doc with request shapes by tomorrow EOD.
[06:07] Lena Wu: On the private deployment option — is there an on-prem appliance or is it mostly VPC-based? A couple of our accounts insist on on-prem.
[06:16] Ethan Park: We offer both. V P C deployment is the faster route for partners; we also ship an on-prem package for air-gapped installs. On-prem has longer lead times (hardware procurement) but gives full control.
[06:29] Diane Morales: Any red flags for EU data that you foresee? E.g., telemetry leaving region or logging defaults?
[06:35] Ethan Park: The main things are telemetry and analytics — our control plane can be configured for region-only retention for logs and audit trails. For full guarantees we can move to Private. Also KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) stop us from seeing plaintext. We'll document those options.
[06:50] Marina Patel: Let's talk about go-to-market — Diane, what's your preferred sequence for joint outreach? Warm intro vs joint webinar vs co-branded case study?
[06:58] Diane Morales: Warm intro first for the top two accounts. For the wider list a joint webinar targeted at platform vendors in EU would be great but that's an FY initiative.
[07:07] Marina Patel: Ok warm intros for Account A and C. Who are the champions there?
[07:11] Diane Morales: Account A champion is Marco (Head of Engineering), Account C champion is Petra (Head of Product). We'll share names and contact emails in the doc.
[07:19] Arjun Singh: On the pilot logistics, what success metrics should we propose? Latency under X ms for 95th, throughput Y rps, and error rate < 0.5%?
[07:28] Ethan Park: Yes that's sensible. For the fintech customer I'd propose p95 < 350ms for 512-token responses and throughput target of 100 concurrent sessions as a pilot baseline. We can show cost per 1k tokens on the run.
[07:41] Lena Wu: Sounds good. Also we need a rollback/fallback plan — if the pilot shows higher latency, do you have automatic fallbacks to cheaper variants?
[07:49] Ethan Park: We have smart routing and fallback policies; you can route to a compatible smaller model or another region. Redwood's runtime supports automatic model fallback in case of capacity constraints. There will be slight change in output characteristics and we flag that in the SLO.
[08:04] Diane Morales: One more legal question — for joint accounts who signs the data processing addendum? CloudArc or the end customer?
[08:12] Marina Patel: Typically the end customer signs the DPA with Redwood and CloudArc signs a partner agreement with Redwood. We can adapt if the legal teams want a different arrangement. We'll surface examples in the contract templates.
[08:24] Arjun Singh: Competitor question — a few prospects asked about Nebula AI; how is Redwood different?
[08:29] Marina Patel: Short answer: Redwood focuses on production inferencing economics and deployment flexibility — we provide explicit options for Dedicated and Private with observability and batching optimizations. Nebula tends to be more research-oriented, less ops focus — ModelServe sells wider model catalog but with less tooling for rollout and observability. We'll include a short competitor positioning slide.
[08:50] Diane Morales: Helpful.
[08:53] Marina Patel: Ok want to run a quick recap and next steps so everyone is aligned?
[08:58] Diane Morales: Sure.
[09:00] Marina Patel: Recap: 1) Redwood to send co-sell deck, partner one-pager, security pack (SOC2, KMS, VPC options) by 2026-04-06. 2) CloudArc to share sanitized payloads and traffic shapes by 2026-04-04. 3) Ethan to run perf baseline in EU with the provided payloads and deliver p50/p95/throughput/cost spreadsheet by 2026-04-09. 4) Schedule exec intro with channel sales — target week of 2026-04-13. 5) Diane to share champion contacts for Account A and C by 2026-04-08.
[09:33] Diane Morales: That all looks right. Anything else?
[09:37] Lena Wu: If you could call out the KV caching defaults and any PII controls in the security pack that would be helpful.
[09:44] Ethan Park: I'll add a small appendix in the perf results explaining caching knobs and how to disable persistent caching.
[09:50] Marina Patel: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
[09:54] Diane Morales: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:56] Arjun Singh: Thanks all.
[09:58] Lena Wu: Bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("V P C" typed as VPC sometimes, "K V cash" noted in transcript), minor speaker overlaps, typical Fireflies imperfect punctuation.
